scope: same main20 windows as the published both operator curves; 8 ranks x 20 cycles
interpretation: Inferred dominant pipeline activity only, not a proven critical-path or bandwidth bottleneck; no claims for unannotated batches.
method: For each kernel instance, approximate active time = corresponding AIC/AIV engine time * pipeline cycle ratio. For MTE2 and Scalar take max(AIC contribution,AIV contribution) because engines may overlap; aggregate over matching kernels, 8 ranks x 20 main forwards; divide by summed kernel duration. This is a display heuristic; mean time times mean ratio is only a proxy, not per-core critical-path analysis.
ambiguity: Show both pipelines when within 10% of the maximum; Mixed for three or more; add ? when maximum proxy is below 0.30. These are visualization heuristics, not hardware thresholds. Fixpipe/MTE1/MTE3 are also considered to avoid forcing four-way labels.
limitations: Pipeline activity is not proof of a limiting resource. Scalar may include polling/synchronization; high MTE2 does not establish HBM-bandwidth saturation.
Aggregates can hide different call shapes, rank/core imbalance and phase transitions. Unannotated batches are not classified.
Bottom full-model ITL combines operators, communication and waiting; it receives no single pipeline label.
